records.name: Grounded theory
records.scope: Theory-building through variant-specific category development and theoretical sampling.
records.definition: A family of approaches that develops an explanatory, substantive account from sustained comparative analysis.
records.epistemology: Variant-specific; the selected grounded-theory tradition must be explicit.
records.research_questions: Process, action, interaction, and conceptual explanation questions.
records.sampling: Purposive then theoretical sampling; no generic saturation declaration.
records.collection: Iterative collection and analysis with an audit trail.
records.quality: Conceptual integration, negative cases, theoretical sensitivity and variant coherence.
records.ai_constraints: May retrieve comparison material and candidate contrasts; cannot integrate theory, decide sampling, or declare saturation.

records.name: Situational analysis
records.scope: Relational mapping approach, distinct from grounded theory.
records.definition: Analysis of human, non-human, discursive and institutional relations in a situation.
records.research_questions: Questions about relations, positions, silences and social worlds.
records.sampling: Situation and relation boundaries are explicit.
records.collection: Multi-source material may be mapped without treating the map as a final finding.
records.ai_constraints: May organise source metadata; mapping interpretation remains human-led.

records.name: Reflexive thematic analysis
records.scope: Interpretive patterned-meaning analysis; distinct from codebook and coding-reliability thematic approaches.
records.definition: Researcher-generated themes developed through reflexive engagement with a defined dataset.
records.epistemology: Interpretive; researcher subjectivity is an analytic resource requiring reflexive accountability.
records.research_questions: Shared meaning and patterned experience within a defined context.
records.sampling: Dataset scope and information richness, not a universal saturation rule.
records.collection: Collection context and researcher role are retained.
records.quality: Conceptual coherence, reflexivity, contextual adequacy and negative-case engagement.
records.ai_constraints: Retrieval and counterexample prompts only. No automatic themes, consensus coding, kappa or intercoder-reliability recommendation.

records.name: Codebook and coding-reliability thematic analysis
records.scope: Structured thematic approaches with explicit, stable coding procedures.
records.definition: Thematic analysis whose coding rules and quality procedures are specified in advance or collaboratively maintained.
records.epistemology: Varies by design; it is not reflexive thematic analysis by another name.
records.research_questions: Applied comparative questions needing structured code use.
records.sampling: Defined corpus or sample coverage rationale.
records.collection: Comparable material and documented codebook revisions.
records.quality: Codebook transparency and, only where designed for it, calibration/agreement.
records.ai_constraints: May assist stable-codebook application and retrieval; final coding and codebook changes require human review.

records.name: Framework method / framework analysis
records.scope: Systematic matrix-based analysis while preserving case and context.
records.definition: Charting material by case and analytic domain to support transparent comparison.
records.epistemology: Applied and transparent; not a generic theme generator.
records.research_questions: Questions requiring within- and cross-case comparison.
records.sampling: Case and domain coverage are explicit.
records.collection: Structured collection may be combined with emergent analytic work.
records.quality: Matrix traceability, contextual reading, empty and contradictory cells.
records.ai_constraints: May assist organisation and retrieval; human judgement protects case context and category meaning.

records.name: Narrative inquiry and narrative analysis
records.scope: Story, temporality, voice and form are analytic rather than incidental.
records.definition: Analysis that preserves narratives as situated accounts rather than merely segmented code fragments.
records.research_questions: Experience, identity, temporality, storytelling and meaning-making.
records.collection: Whole-story and performance context remain available.
records.quality: Narrative form, voice and context are retained.
records.ai_constraints: May assist chronology retrieval; must not flatten stories into generic themes or overwrite voice.

records.name: Conversation analysis
records.scope: Sequential interactional analysis, not generic thematic analysis.
records.definition: Analysis of practices demonstrable in detailed interactional sequences.
records.epistemology: Interactional and evidence-led through next-turn/sequential proof.
records.collection: Detailed, human-verified transcription and recording context.
records.quality: Sequence, next-turn evidence and deviant-case analysis.
records.ai_constraints: May index verified transcript metadata only. No generic summarisation, coding or theme generation.

records.name: Phenomenological inquiry and interpretative phenomenological analysis
records.scope: Lived experience with variant-specific phenomenological commitments.
records.definition: Idiographic or phenomenological inquiry that interprets experiential meaning without making prevalence claims.
records.research_questions: How people experience and make sense of a phenomenon.
records.sampling: Direct experience; IPA is idiographic and often relatively homogeneous.
records.collection: Deep experiential accounts and contextual interpretation.
records.quality: Idiographic depth, phenomenological/interpretive coherence and reflexivity.
records.ai_constraints: May support retrieval; cannot replace idiographic interpretation or claim prevalence.

records.name: Participatory, action, co-produced and engaged research
records.scope: Research whose decision rights, governance and benefits are shared with participants or communities.
records.definition: Approaches that make power, participation and action central methodological commitments.
records.research_questions: Questions defined or governed with affected communities.
records.sampling: Participation, representation and exclusion are community-governed.
records.collection: Collaborative data generation and action cycles.
records.quality: Decision rights, accountability, dissent and benefit-sharing.
records.ai_constraints: AI cannot determine participation, consent, governance, representation or action priorities.

records.name: Mixed methods and triangulation
records.scope: Deliberate integration of qualitative and quantitative strands.
records.definition: A design requiring explicit integration rather than parallel methods listed together.
records.epistemology: Pragmatic or paradigm-explicit; integration logic must be stated.
records.research_questions: Questions needing complementary forms of evidence.
records.collection: Explicit timing, priority and linkage between strands.
records.ai_constraints: May retrieve and compare material; cannot infer integration or reconcile divergence automatically.

disagreements.title: Grounded-theory emergence, procedure and construction
disagreements.warning: Select and document the grounded-theory variant; do not combine variants as interchangeable procedures.

disagreements.title: Themes emerge versus themes are generated
disagreements.warning: For reflexive thematic analysis, themes are researcher-generated through reflexive engagement, not automatically discovered.

disagreements.title: Intercoder reliability
disagreements.warning: Do not impose agreement metrics on reflexive thematic analysis; use them only where the selected structured approach justifies them.

disagreements.title: Counting and prevalence
disagreements.warning: Frequency never alone establishes qualitative importance or population prevalence.

disagreements.title: Universal qualitative quality criteria
disagreements.warning: Apply method-specific quality criteria rather than one generic checklist.

disagreements.title: AI as clerical tool, analytic collaborator or autonomous analyst
disagreements.warning: AI outputs stay machine-assisted suggestions and require human acceptance, revision or rejection.
